decisions.rationale: 'familial adenomatous polyposis' names one defined specific disease (FAP) and is not used as a modifier of another noun in the title.
'colorectal tumorigenesis' refers to a biological process (tumor formation), not a disease mention.
'familial APC' is the long form naming the same specific disease as the abbreviation FAP in 'familial APC (FAP)'; long form and abbreviation are annotated as separate synonymous mentions.
'FAP' is the abbreviation for familial adenomatous polyposis, annotated as its own mention alongside the long form.
'colorectal adenomas' denotes one defined disease entity (colorectal adenoma) rather than a family of multiple specific diseases, and it is not modifying another noun.
'carcinomas' is a broad family covering many specific cancer types rather than one defined disease.
'disease' is a very general term that is explicitly excluded from annotation.
'severe polyposis' denotes a severity form within the polyposis family, which groups multiple specific diseases, so it is a Disease Class rather than one specific disease.
'attenuated polyposis' denotes a milder form within the polyposis family, which groups multiple specific diseases, so it is a Disease Class.
'FAP' here modifies the noun 'patients' ('FAP patients'), so it is used as a Modifier for another concept.
'colorectal tumor' modifies the noun 'growth' ('colorectal tumor growth'), functioning as a Modifier similar to 'colorectal cancer' in the guideline example.
